usageNotes: Use this to configure which ACME account and domain(s) the PDM node should use for automatic TLS certificate issuance. Requires System.Modify privilege. The `digest` param should be supplied (read from GET /config first) to prevent a lost-update race if multiple admins could modify config concurrently; omitting it is safe in single-admin environments.

examples.summary: Configure ACME with a primary domain using HTTP validation and a secondary domain via DNS plugin

tips: acmedomain0 through acmedomain4 allow up to five SANs on a single certificate; acmedomain0 typically becomes the CN.
Omitting the plugin sub-key on a domain entry defaults to standalone HTTP validation — ensure port 80 is reachable from the ACME CA for that challenge to succeed.
Use the alias sub-key when _acme-challenge DNS records are delegated to a separate zone via CNAME, so the plugin writes the TXT record to the aliased domain instead.
After updating this config, trigger actual certificate issuance or renewal via the certificate order/renew endpoint; this PUT only saves the configuration, it does not immediately contact the CA.
Pass the `delete` array to remove individual properties (e.g., remove a previously set acmedomain1) without having to resend all values.
